messages.subject: CSV Data Formatting
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Thanks for your incredible work on the package! I am working with iOS and android accelerometer data and I have a csv file( sample attached) with 4 columns: the timestamp, x,y and z coordinates. I learned about read.myacc.csv() for data formatting and I have used with g.shell.GGIR as shown below:

g.shell.GGIR(
  read.myacc.csv(rmc.file="as_project/accelerometer/data/sample.csv",
                 rmc.firstrow.acc = 1,
                 rmc.col.acc = 2:4,
                 rmc.col.temp = c(),
                 rmc.col.time=1,
                 rmc.unit.acc = "g",
                 rmc.unit.temp = "C",
                 rmc.unit.time = "POSIX",
                 rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
                 rmc.bitrate = c(),
                 #rmc.dynamic_range = 6,
                # rmc.unsignedbit = TRUE,
                 rmc.origin = "1970-01-01",
                 rmc.desiredtz = "America/New_York",
                # rmc.sf = 100,
                # rmc.headername.sf = c(),
                # rmc.headername.sn = c(),
                 #rmc.headername.recordingid = c(),
                # rmc.header.structure = c(),
                 #rmc.check4timegaps = FALSE,
                 rmc.col.wear = c(),
                 rmc.doresample=FALSE
                ),
  mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
 # datadir="as_project/accelerometer/data/sample.csv",
  outputdir="/Volumes/Columbia/R21_Passive_Sensor/as_project/accelerometer/output",
  do.report=c(2,4,5),
  studyname = "test",
  overwrite = FALSE,
  
  # Part 1
  #-------------------------------
  windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),           
  do.cal = TRUE,
  do.enmo = TRUE,            
  do.anglex=TRUE,             
  do.angley=TRUE,            
  do.anglez=TRUE,            
  chunksize=1,
  printsummary=TRUE,
  
  
  #=====================
  # Part 2
  #=====================
  strategy = 1,
  hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
  maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,
  qwindow=c(0,24),
  mvpathreshold =c(100),
  bout.metric = 4,
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  includenightcrit = 16,
  
  #=====================
  # Part 3 + 4
  #=====================
  def.noc.sleep = 1,
  outliers.only = TRUE,
  criterror = 4,
  do.visual = TRUE,
  
  #=====================
  # Part 5
  #=====================
  threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
  boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
  #=====================
  # Visual report
  #=====================
  timewindow = c("WW"),
  visualreport=TRUE)


However, I get the error shown below:

Error in data.table::fread(rmc.file, nrow = rmc.nrow, skip = skip, dec = rmc.dec,  : 
  is.numeric(nrows) is not TRUE

Can you please help me diagnose this? Thank you so much!

Best,
Apoorva

parts:
Hi Apoorva,
You are nearly there. Instead of providing the entire function as input to g.shell.GGIR you should only provide the read.myacc.csv arguments as input to g.shell.GGIR, but leave out the line:
rmc.file="as_project/accelerometer/data/sample.csv",

So, it would then look as follows:
g.shell.GGIR(     rmc.firstrow.acc = 1,

rmc.col.acc = 2:4,
                 rmc.col.temp = c(),
                 rmc.col.time=1,
                 rmc.unit.acc = "g",
                 rmc.unit.temp = "C",
                 rmc.unit.time = "POSIX",
                 rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
                 rmc.bitrate = c(),
                 #rmc.dynamic_range = 6,
                # rmc.unsignedbit = TRUE,
                 rmc.origin = "1970-01-01",
                 rmc.desiredtz = "America/New_York",
                # rmc.sf = 100,
                # rmc.headername.sf = c(),
                # rmc.headername.sn = c(),
                 #rmc.headername.recordingid = c(),
                # rmc.header.structure = c(),
                 #rmc.check4timegaps = FALSE,
                 rmc.col.wear = c(),
rmc.doresample=FALSE,

mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
 # datadir="as_project/accelerometer/data/sample.csv",
  outputdir="/Volumes/Columbia/R21_Passive_Sensor/as_project/accelerometer/output",
  do.report=c(2,4,5),
  studyname = "test",

overwrite = FALSE, ... code continued see original message
